newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's left launches new challenge to CVRD sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's left launches new challenge to CVRD sale.

text.p: Three Brazilian left-wing political parties have lodged a new constitutional challenge to the government's plan to privatize Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
The parties filed a so-called Inconstutional Action at the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), Brazil's highest court on constitutional matters, a court spokeswoman said.
The spokeswoman said she did not know the motive for the challenge.
Newswire Invest News said the parties alleged the involvement of foreign capital in consortia due to bid for voting shares in CVRD meant Senate approval was needed for the CVRD privatization.

The STF has rejected several Inconstitutional Actions lodged by opponents of the CVRD selloff over the last couple of weeks. But a judge at the court upheld one challenge which suspended the transfer of part of the Carajas mining complex to CVRD.

The STF case would not be affected by a possible injunction being mulled in the Superior Justice Tribunbal (STJ) in the latest twist of a legal battle between the government and opponents of the CVRD privatization.

The government has asked an STJ judge to issue an injunction grouping all cases involving injunctions against the CVRD auction in one court. The judge might also rule that all the injunctions are invalid.
